text:
Maria (runtime): quick heads-up: observed a repeating tail pattern during tenant lane reshuffles — not a p99 regression but short 30-120ms spikes for streaming tokens when hot tenants are moved.
Devon: yeah, saw that. looks like kernel rebind + kvcache churn on handoff.
Lee: can you paste a tiny trace?
Maria (runtime):
```
[10:05:33] req T enters lane-7
[10:05:34] hot tenant H moved -> lane-2
[10:05:34] kernel swap + kvcache rebind -> stall ~90ms
[10:05:36] stream resumes
```
Sasha: that rebind cost is the main suspect. options: (A) throttle moves of hot tenants, (B) keep an "anchor" noop to preserve residency, (C) reserved lanes for critical tenants.
Devon: anchors seem promising but cost batch capacity. we should cap them via an anchor_token_pool per-GPU.
Lee: propose lightweight telemetry first: emit a handoff_tail metric (sampled) that measures median delta pre/post handoff per-tenant. sampling 1/20 handoffs.
Maria (runtime): prototype anchor config idea:
```
anchor_pool:
  per_gpu: 8
  token_cost: 1
  refill_policy: adaptive
```
Sasha: I'll add a simulator flag (--model-anchors) that treats anchors as +1 token and models rebind cost. lets replay.
Devon: tradeoffs to document: anchors reduce jitter but consume shaping capacity; delaying moves reduces churn but can add latency to moved tenant; reserved lanes solve it but cost infra. per-SLA defaults required.
Maria (runtime): action items: Sasha -> sampler + simulator; Lee -> PromQL for handoff_tail panel; Devon -> replay job; I'll draft policy defaults and rollout notes. infra-bot: FYI canary deploy at 16:00 UTC.
Devon: noted, will watch metrics during canary.
Maria (runtime): thanks — keep alerts on handoff_tail > 30ms for heavy tenants. :eyes:
